_comment: Language-NEUTRAL structured-data facts, single source of truth for the index + competition + workshop + contact JSON-LD. Values are copied verbatim from the live JSON-LD blocks; do not 'improve' them. Translatable strings (names/descriptions/labels) live in _data/i18n/<lang>.json.
_commentEventDates: startDate and eventPublishStartDate MUST be kept identical. eleventyComputed.js emits the index/competition Event using eventPublishStartDate; startDate is the neutral fact and the proxy guard. Changing one without the other silently publishes a stale date. Adding eventPublishStartDate is what OPENS the index/competition Event gate; removing it re-closes it.
_commentWorkshop: Reference data for the workshop Event JSON-LD, which is DATE-GATED: eleventyComputed.js emits the workshop Event only once a real `workshopStartDate` (and optionally `workshopEndDate`) is added here — until then the workshop page carries only Organization + BreadcrumbList. (An undated Event, and its undated/locationless subEvents, are invalid rich results, so the placeholder talk/panel subEvents were dropped; re-add only REAL dated subEvents on restore.) The fields below stay as the neutral facts for that future restore: own attendance mode (Offline, vs the index/competition Mixed); `organizer` Hamburg + CMU; the panel `performer` list (proper nouns + affiliations). Translatable strings (event name/description, the former talk/panel subEvent names) live in i18n/<lang>.json jsonld.*.
_commentOpenDayHamburg: Neutral facts for the Hamburg Open Day Event JSON-LD on open-day-hamburg.html, DATE-GATED on openDayHamburgStartDate in the same way as the workshop gate — but unlike the workshop Event, this one has a REAL date and a REAL venue, so the gate is open and a valid Event is emitted today. This is independent of the index/competition Event gate (eventPublishStartDate), which opened on 2026-07-22 when the revised schedule was locked — do not couple them. Talk-level subEvents are deliberately omitted, but NO LONGER because the titles are missing — that precondition expired when the program was revised. Each of the three morning talks now carries a confirmed title and a named speaker (the transfers, lunch, site visit and lab visits have no speaker, correctly), so the subEvents COULD be built today: the omission is a standing editorial choice, not a data gap, exactly the position the Shanghai keys reached first. Do not re-derive it as 'titles are TBA'. If they are ever added, each needs a real name/startDate/endDate/location — an Event node without those is an invalid rich result, the same reasoning that dropped the workshop's placeholder subEvents — and tests/baseline/open-day-hamburg.html must be re-cut in the same commit; that one fixture only, since the /zh/ mirror has no golden (verify-zh asserts invariants, not goldens). Translatable strings (event name/description, breadcrumb) live in i18n/<lang>.json jsonld.*.
_commentOpenDayShanghai: Neutral facts for the Shanghai Open Day Event JSON-LD on open-day-shanghai.html, DATE-GATED on openDayShanghaiStartDate in the same way as the Hamburg gate. Independent of both the Hamburg gate and the index/competition gate (eventPublishStartDate) — do not couple them. Times are China Standard Time (UTC+08:00). Talk-level subEvents are deliberately omitted. On this page every slot carries a confirmed name and each of the four talks a named speaker (the break, site visit and dinner have no speaker, correctly), and there is no 16:30 slot at all since the revised program. So the omission is now a standing editorial choice, not a data gap: the subEvents COULD be built today. If they are ever added, each needs a real name/startDate/endDate/location, and tests/baseline/open-day-shanghai.html must be re-cut in the same commit — that one fixture only: the Open Day hub emits no Event, and the /zh/ mirror's Event changes too but has no golden fixture (verify-zh asserts invariants, not goldens). Hamburg's keys now hold the same position for the same reason — its talk titles were confirmed when its program was revised — so there is no TBA rationale left on either event to copy back and forth. The event is invitation-only, so no Offer node is emitted — an Offer with price 0 would wrongly signal open public admission. postalCode is omitted rather than guessed. addressRegion is deliberately ABSENT, and the district instead rides in streetAddress: schema.org's addressRegion is a FIRST-LEVEL administrative division, and Shanghai is itself that division — Minhang is a district beneath it. Do not copy the pattern from the Pittsburgh testbedAddresses row above (addressRegion 'PA'), where the region genuinely is first-level. The venue is hosted by Franka Robotics' Shanghai office, and the EBiM Shanghai testbed is in the same building — so the Place carries the host's name while organizer names the EBiM lead organizing institution, exactly as the Hamburg keys do for Google Germany GmbH. Hosting a venue is not organizing the event; do not move Franka Robotics into organizer. Translatable strings live in i18n/<lang>.json jsonld.*. NOTE openDayShanghaiUrl is currently UNCONSUMED and that is deliberate, not an oversight: its Hamburg twin openDayHamburgUrl is read only by that page's offers.url, and this event emits no Offer, so nothing reads this key today. It is retained as the neutral canonical-URL fact (the same way the workshop* keys are retained for a future restore) — the Event's own `url` comes from the page's canonical, not from here. Do not 'fix' the asymmetry by adding an Offer.
